Using approximately 37 inverse femtobarns of proton-proton collision data collected at $\sqrt{s}= 8$ TeV by the LHCb detector, an effective lifetime measurement for the ${{B^0_s}\rightarrow K^+K^-}$ decay has been achieved. Derived directly from the exponential decay probability distribution of the ${{B^0_s}\rightarrow K^+K^-}$ sample, this effective lifetime, denoted as $c{ {\tau_{eff}}({{\rm{}}B^0_s}\rightarrow K^+K^-)}$, is determined to be $0.082 \pm 0.004 \text{(stat)} \pm 0.006 \text{(syst)}$.

This study examines the numerical discretization of an optimal stochastic control problem involving the differential operators introduced by Da Prato and Zabczyk. These operators act on a product space comprising a Hilbert space and a H\"{o}mmer-Lie algebra. The study introduces a numerical scheme that approximates the stochastic differential equation associated with the problem. The authors demonstrate that the state space of the problem is not uniquely ergodic and demonstrate that the target function of the optimal control problem is not unique. The study demonstrates that the numerical solution converges to a target function that is optimal.

This study examines charged particle spectra and the nuclear modification factor ($R_{AA}$) across a wide transverse momentum range ($0.5 < p_{\mathrm{T}} < 50$ GeV/c) for both electrons and charged hadrons in $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.02$ TeV p+Pb collisions at ATLAS. The dataset comprises $N_{\mathrm{e}}=1.1 \times 10^{6}$ p+Pb events at mid-rapidity ($|y|<2.5$) with an integrated luminosity of $1.0 \, \mathrm{nb}^{-1}$, collected during the LHC's 2016 data-taking run. The analysis compares results from p+Pb interactions against d+Au and p+p reference collisions. The findings indicate that charged particle yields in p+Pb collisions are approximately $10$ times higher than those observed in d+Au events. Additionally, the analysis presents the first $R_{AA}$ measurement for electrons at this energy in p+Pb collisions, showing strong consistency with the charged hadron spectrum.

We examine the quantum mechanics associated with the complexification of select finite-dimensional Lie algebras, focusing on their harmonic oscillators and path integrals. Our findings reveal that for several such systems, the resulting noncommutative quantum mechanics can be reformulated as standard quantum mechanics involving a higher-dimensional harmonic oscillator.

The proportion of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) serves as a significant prognostic factor for cancer patients and is a key target for improving the accuracy of predictive models. However, generating such models is challenging because the computation required to segment TILs from histopathology images is highly resource-intensive. This study introduces a new dataset comprising 1,000 whole-slide images annotated with TIL proportions, derived from breast cancer resection samples. Additionally, we develop a deep-learning model designed to classify TIL levels using only coarse, text-based labels. To facilitate this, we introduce a novel whole-slide image (WSI) encoding technique that aggregates image-level embeddings into a compact representation, enabling efficient batch processing. Finally, we train this model using federated learning across ten institutions, utilizing only 10% of the labels for each image. The resulting classifier achieves a macro F1 score of 0.81, demonstrating that this approach can effectively classify TIL proportions with high precision.

This study examines decision-feedback equalization (DFE) in a field-deployed submarine fiber-optic link, analyzing how linear impairments such as chromatic dispersion and modal noise interact with nonlinear effects like four-wave mixing and cross-phase modulation. By analyzing the linear channel response, we identify that DFE can suppress nonlinear interference (NLI) at specific frequencies, yet this suppression inadvertently amplifies NLI at others. The findings reveal that burst error propagation in the time domain corresponds directly to this frequency-domain amplification. Consequently, the research proposes a novel NLI mitigation strategy: inserting a pre-equalizer prior to the main DFE to eliminate the burst errors. Experimental results confirm that this approach reduces the Q-factor penalty by 0.4 dB across various modulation formats and transmission distances.

Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) have emerged as a potent alternative to Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) for time-series analysis, offering comparable performance while maintaining a streamlined design. Nevertheless, their substantial parameter counts and computational complexity pose significant challenges for deployment on resource-constrained devices. To address this, we introduce a novel lightweight network architecture optimizer for TCNs, named Pruning in Time (PIT). PIT operates by iteratively applying layer-wise pruning and fine-tuning, guided by a newly defined metric called Temporal Importance (TI). Unlike existing methods that rely on global pruning strategies, PIT leverages the inductive biases inherent in TCNs to perform more effective layer-specific adjustments. Comprehensive evaluations on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that PIT outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques, delivering superior performance with reduced computational costs.

This work presents the proof that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra defined over any field exhibits a null structure. This finding is derived as a consequence of a more general theorem concerning the related class of commutative conformal commutators.

This study examines fluctuations in the initial spatial and momentum anisotropy, denoted as $\psi_s$ and $\psi_s$ respectively, within the initial state of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP). These fluctuations are inferred by comparing them to those of the final-state QGP and the resulting hadronic matter. The research analyzes data from Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 5.02 TeV collected by the ALICE detector at the LHC. The findings reveal that the spatial and momentum fluctuations in the initial state are consistent with each other, yet the final-state spatial and momentum fluctuations exhibit a discrepancy. The study attributes this divergence to the influence of initial-state momentum fluctuations on the final state, which is supported by hydrodynamic simulations.

This paper investigates the correspondence theory of first-order definable dual logic algebra semantics, encompassing both intuitionistic and classical settings. It introduces a novel, unitary approach to determine the complete first-order correspondent for any single-premise valid dual logic algebra principle. This method relies on the concept of the canonical prime filter correspondence matrix associated with such principles.

This paper introduces a new approach to managing table data containing null values and functional dependencies. It defines a specific class of tables that remain free of spurious functional dependencies when considering only non-null values, and demonstrates that any table within this category can be decomposed into a set of smaller, related tables. This decomposition process functions similarly to 3NF synthesis but accommodates nulls by utilizing functional dependencies that are valid for the entire table. Furthermore, the study defines a specific 3NF candidate key that generalizes the traditional concept of a superkey.

By allowing autoregressive coefficients to evolve over time, this framework offers greater flexibility than constant-coefficient models. We derive the theoretical properties of TV-PAR and propose a smoothing algorithm to estimate these time-varying parameters. We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), a novel approach for representing object states during robotic manipulation. Unlike many existing methods, NDFs do not require object-specific training and are differentiable, supporting end-to-end optimization. By integrating point-wise descriptors with neural networks, NDFs generate a continuous, differentiable representation of an object's state that is SE(3)-equivariant, allowing them to generalize across arbitrary object poses without needing object instance segmentation masks. We demonstrate the utility of NDFs in estimating object states for tasks such as pushing and placing, where end-to-end optimized policies utilizing NDFs achieve performance comparable to state-of-the-art techniques. Furthermore, we establish that NDFs are highly data-efficient, requiring only a single image per object for training.

The SiD detector, developed by the SiD collaboration, is designed for the upgraded International Linear Collider (ILC). This next-generation machine will operate with significantly higher luminosity, specifically a luminosity upgrade (LU) to $2 \times 10^{35} \text{ cm}^{-2} \text{ s}^{-1}$. The ILC's primary mission involves exploring the Standard Model (SM) in profound detail, searching for new physics beyond it, and investigating the origin of electroweak symmetry breaking. To achieve these goals, the SiD detector must achieve exceptional precision in measuring SM processes and possess the sensitivity to discover new phenomena. This paper outlines the updated SiD detector concept, which incorporates a luminosity upgrade to support these scientific objectives.

We present the third installment of the Bulge Cluster APOgee Survey (CAPOS III), which identifies 10 new Milky Way globular clusters (GCs) in the Galactic bulge region. Our primary focus is Tonantzintla 2 (Ton 2), a newly discovered cluster with a heliocentric distance of 8.1 kpc and a line-of-sight velocity of 211 km/s. Spectroscopic analysis reveals that Ton 2 exhibits metal-poor characteristics, with [Fe/H] = -1.21 ± 0.04 dex and an alpha-enhancement of approximately +0.3 dex. Based on the isochrones, the cluster's age is estimated at 11.5 ± 1.5 Gyr. Kinematic analysis places Ton 2 within the bulge population, as it resides near the peak of the bulge velocity distribution and aligns with the bulge's rotation curve. Furthermore, the cluster's position in the color-magnitude diagram and its location in the color-[Fe/H] diagram suggest it belongs to the bulge's main stellar population. The derived radial velocity, combined with previously published proper motions, yields a total space velocity of 240 km/s. The Isabelle/2005 release introduced a file-organization tool designed to enhance the usability of the Isabelle Archive of Formal Proofs (IFOP). This tool enables users to browse proofs by mathematical domain, browse by specific theories, and search for files containing particular keywords. This paper examines the structural characteristics of the IFOP to evaluate the tool's effectiveness. It details the methodology used to analyze the archive's structure and presents initial findings. Furthermore, it outlines several enhancements to the tool that were implemented based on these insights.

By applying the conformal field theory framework, we derive a universal formula for the complex plane position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity within standard O(N) universality classes. Our findings indicate that across all O(N) critical systems, this singularity adheres to a unified scaling law: $z_{Y\!L} = -\exp\left[\frac{2\pi}{c_{\rm CFT}}\right]$, where $z_{\rm YL}$ is the Yang-Lee singularity position and $c_{\rm CFT}$ is the central charge. This theoretical prediction aligns with numerical results from Monte Carlo simulations for the Ising, XY, and Heisenberg universality classes.

We introduce a novel lemma that extends the Sudakov-Fernique inequality to functions of Gaussian vectors with independent components, where each component's distribution depends on its index. Utilizing this lemma, we establish a new proof of the convergence result for the free energy within the fully connected spherical spin model, specifically addressing the Nishimori phase diagram. Our approach is entirely local in nature, thereby circumventing the need for the previously required global convexity of the TAP free energy.

Metasurfaces represent a two-dimensional variant of metamaterials, renowned for manipulating electromagnetic waves through spatially varying surface impedance. While experimental and numerical techniques have traditionally dominated research, this paper introduces a rigorous analytical framework for metasurfaces. By deriving impedance surface equations and applying impedance sheet theory, the study addresses surface wave propagation and surface plasmons. Furthermore, it analyzes surface scattering by integrating impedance sheet theory with the generalized Snell's law. Finally, the proposed methodology is validated through specific examples, demonstrating its utility in guiding future metasurface designs.

This study investigates smooth orbital linearization for smooth integrable vector fields featuring a complete first integral. We establish that such orbital linearization is achievable near a compact hyperbolic regular level set if and only if the stable and unstable manifolds associated with every hyperbolic singularity conform to specific geometric constraints relative to the level sets of the integral. As a result, we derive orbital linearization for smooth germs of integrable vector fields possessing a non-degenerate Birkhoff–Poincaré integral.

We introduce ElectronCorrNet, a deep learning framework designed to train electron density models that learn energy functionals specifically tuned to capture full electron correlation within the full configuration interaction (FCI) setting. Evaluated across several molecular systems, ElectronCorrNet generates highly accurate electronic density models even when restricted to single-reference, FCI-restricted scenarios. When integrated with Kohn-Sham (KS) methods, these models facilitate rapid and precise calculations of molecular properties, including those for challenging cases like the nitrogen molecule ($N_2$). Furthermore, we demonstrate that ElectronCorrNet-derived densities can effectively support active learning strategies for developing machine-learned interatomic potentials.

We report the discovery of a massive HII region arc in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC), designated N40W, which spans approximately 1.5 kiloparsecs in radius and 100 parsecs in width. This structure is situated near the LMC's southern edge, roughly 1.5 kiloparsecs away from the dwarf galaxy's center. Observations reveal that N40W W exhibits a peak radio flux density of 1.5 Jy at 1.4 GHz, with a spectral index of -0.6. The arc's temperature is estimated to be 10,000 Kelvin, and its total mass is approximately 100,000 solar masses. The radio emission is likely powered by a massive O-type star located at the arc's northern end, with a candidate identified as HSC J0514-6956. The formation mechanism of N40W W remains uncertain, though it may have been triggered by the LMC's tidal forces or the gravitational influence of the Milky Way.

This study examines the application of stellar photometry for measuring planetary-scale aerosols, utilizing a 0.4-meter telescope equipped with a 1000-slit transmission grating spectrophotometer. The instrument's spectral response was calibrated using a high-precision transmission standard, and its spectral sensitivity was mapped to derive the airmass-dependent response curves of standard photometric systems. By analyzing the spectral energy distributions of stars across varying airmasses, the research quantifies aerosol optical depth (AOD) at a 550 nm wavelength ($\tau_{550}$) via the Langley method. The derived AOD values were cross-validated against concurrent satellite data from the MODIS instrument on the Terra platform. The analysis indicates that the spectral slope of atmospheric attenuation aligns with the Angström exponent ($\alpha$), which characterizes the size distribution of aerosols. Consequently, this technique offers a viable means to monitor aerosols over regional and planetary scales.

The origins of peridynamics trace back to the 1930s, yet its resurgence as a viable theory for modeling fracture mechanics occurred only in the mid-1990s. This paper examines the fundamental tenets of bond-based peridynamics, highlighting its core distinction from conventional continuum theories: the reliance on nonlocal interactions. By substituting local dependencies with spatially extended integrals, bond-based peridynamics achieves a one-to-micro mapping between material behavior and bond properties. This approach yields a theoretical framework where the number of independent parameters remains finite, thereby ensuring mathematical tractability. However, this restriction to a finite parameter set inherently constrains the theory's capacity to capture the full breadth of complex material phenomena.

Extending the concept of bond-based peridynamics to fluid dynamics presents a novel and promising avenue. This work introduces a new nonlocal theory specifically formulated for fluid mechanics, grounded in the generalized peridynamic energy functional. This functional incorporates both a nonlocal kinetic energy component and a nonlocal bond energy term. Within this theoretical structure, the kinetic energy accounts for relative motions between fluid particles, while the bond energy is derived from a nonlocal extension of Helmholtz free energy. By applying the variational principle to this functional, the authors derive the corresponding nonlocal theory of fluid dynamics. The resulting governing equations consist of a nonlocal peridynamic momentum balance and a nonlocal peridynamic entropy inequality. These formulations yield a generalized, nonlocal

We introduce GGLasso, a Python library designed to solve the general Graphical Lasso problem. This tool enables researchers to work with the broadest possible covariance matrix and precision matrix, encompassing constraints on diagonal elements, specific off-diagonal pairs, and connections between rows and columns. While the CUDDl package can handle many of these constraints, it lacks support for Python integration. In contrast, GGLasso utilizes the Python-based CUDDl interface to generate efficient solvers. We also present performance benchmarks demonstrating that GGLasso outperforms the R package GLASSO in terms of speed.

We introduce a novel algorithm integrating Hamiltonian Langevin Dynamics with the Metropolis-Hastings framework to enhance the sampling efficiency of configurational molecular systems. This approach aims to mitigate the limitations of standard molecular dynamics methods, which often suffer from inadequate sampling due to excessively small acceptance rates. By leveraging the dual advantages of ergodicity inherent in Metropolis-Hastings methods and the rapid convergence rates typical of Hamiltonian Langevin methods, our technique achieves a substantial reduction in the autocorrelation times of energy and atomic position data. Furthermore, our study examines the algorithm's convergence properties and establishes a theoretical upper bound for its asymptotic convergence rate. Numerical experiments across various test cases confirm that the proposed method is both effective and computationally efficient.

We present numerical relativity simulations of binary black hole mergers embedded within an environment of wave dark matter (WDM). Our study focuses on how the post-merger gravitational wave signal is influenced by the surrounding WDM, specifically examining the amplitude of the ringdown phase and the emission of gravitational waves during the inspiral phase. Our results indicate that WDM can significantly alter the ringdown waveform, with the maximum change in the ringdown amplitude reaching approximately 10% when the dark matter's initial amplitude parameter, $\psi_{\rm in}$, is $10^{-5}$. Furthermore, we observe that WDM can modify the total radiated energy and the frequency of the post-merger quasi-normal modes. Specifically, the WDM can shift the frequency of the fundamental $(l,m)=(2,2)$ mode by up to $2\%$ for a $\psi_{\rm in}$ value of $10^{-5}$. Additionally, we find that the presence of WDM can excite higher-order quasi-normal modes, such as the $(l,m)=(3,3)$ mode, with amplitudes as high as $10\%$ of the fundamental mode when $\psi_{\rm in} = 10^{-5}$. These findings suggest that upcoming gravitational wave detectors, such as LIGO and Virgo, may be able to constrain WDM parameters by analyzing the ringdown signals from black hole mergers.

This study investigates the dynamics of an Euler-Bernoulli beam with three stretched vertices on a metric graph configured in a star shape. The study establishes well-posedness for the system and derives exponential decay rates, which are determined by the boundary conditions and the specific metric of the graph. Additionally, the study identifies scenarios where the system fails to exhibit uniform stability.

Acoustic lenses are essential for enhancing the sensitivity of large-area detectors used in photoacoustic tomography (PAT). While PAT generates high-frequency ultrasonic waves from optically excited regions, these detectors must effectively capture signals across a broad frequency spectrum. However, designing lenses that maintain a wide acceptance angle while managing varying focal lengths for different frequencies remains difficult. This study introduces a novel acoustic lens constructed from a silicone-based polymer composite filled with hollow glass microspheres. Experimental results indicate that the lens exhibits strong acoustic impedance matching to water and demonstrates superior sound transmission in the 0.5–4 MHz range. These findings suggest the material is well-suited for next-generation PAT detectors.

We introduce a novel framework for calculating eigenvector centrality in multilayer networks that accounts for the interplay between a node's significance across different layers and the specific allocation of importance within each layer. This approach generalizes the standard multilayer eigenvector centrality model by allowing a node's overall importance to remain distinct from a simple function of its individual layer contributions. Additionally, we propose an adaptive method to determine these node-specific weights. Empirical tests on various datasets demonstrate that our proposed approach outperforms the conventional multilayer model in identifying nodes with high importance.

This study introduces a deep learning framework designed to process raw, unsharpened digital single-lens reflex (DSLR) images. The proposed method jointly learns demosaicing, deblurring, and denoise techniques through a single shared network, utilizing only the raw Bayer data as input. To facilitate this, a new synthetic dataset was created by applying controlled camera simulations that generate realistic blur and noise patterns. Experimental outcomes demonstrate that this approach surpasses existing methods in terms of both quantitative metrics and visual quality. Furthermore, it has been successfully deployed on a physical DSLR system, yielding significant improvements over traditional raw processing workflows.

We derive the relativistic wave equation for a free particle within the $R$-Minkowski spacetime framework, which incorporates a universal minimum length scale. This equation is constructed by applying the Heisenberg-Raich uncertainty relation as a modification to the standard Dirac equation in flat Minkowski spacetime. We demonstrate that the resulting equation is Lorentz covariant and possesses a conserved probability current. Furthermore, we establish the equivalence between the modified Dirac equation and a set of coupled Pauli-Gross type equations. Finally, we derive the energy spectrum associated with this system.

This release introduces a Python-based software package designed to identify causal links among variables within datasets. The package offers a suite of methods for both pairwise and full graph-based causal structure learning, along with visualization tools. It is available for download at https://github.com/CDavis1992/CDavis1992.

This study examines the surface-seal phase of sphere water entry, focusing on the intermediate velocity range where the sphere's radius is comparable to the capillary length. We establish a theoretical framework that integrates the classical potential flow model with a contact line hysteresis approach to determine the impact force. Our findings indicate that the force-time profile exhibits a double-peak structure, with the secondary peak magnitude increasing as velocity rises. Furthermore, our model accurately predicts the primary peak force across various entry speeds, demonstrating strong agreement with both experimental data and numerical simulations.

Generalized theta-terms, which are topological invariants appearing in the low-energy effective field theory of string theory, serve as the primary mechanism for spontaneous global symmetry breaking. We have identified generalized theta-terms corresponding to every possible broken continuous global symmetry within the four-dimensional Type IIB supergravity framework. Our methodology relies on the precise mapping between generalized theta-terms and specific topological terms in the generalized Born-Infeld sector of the theory.

In the realm of virtualized computing, trust is frequently compromised by security flaws within the hardware, software, or both. We propose a novel hardware architecture designed to minimize trust requirements by exclusively utilizing physically isolated instances of virtualized environments. Our approach introduces a new architecture that employs a single, untrusted hardware root to instantiate multiple independent execution realms, each equipped with its own trusted root. This architecture employs hardware-enforced mechanisms to guarantee strict resource partitioning, secure inter-realm communication, and the secure provisioning of resources. We validate the feasibility of our design through a prototype implementation on an FPGA, demonstrating that it effectively isolates various vulnerability classes, including Spectre, Meltdown, and certain side-channel attacks.

In the realm of reinforcement learning, the integrity of learning is frequently compromised by corrupted data. This paper introduces a robust policy gradient algorithm specifically designed to address the challenge of a corrupting adversary who manipulates the rewards associated with sampled transitions. By framing the policy improvement step as a constrained optimization problem, the proposed robust variant achieves strong guarantees: it remains within a small statistical distance of the optimal policy derived through standard policy gradient methods, even when the adversary alters up to a fraction of the data. In contrast, the traditional policy gradient approach yields a significantly suboptimal outcome under such attack conditions. Furthermore, our method demonstrates superior resilience compared to existing robust alternatives, successfully withstanding adversaries capable of strong, data-level manipulation.

We demonstrate a variation of the Box Paradox that eliminates player selection, allowing them to guess coordinates simultaneously. This choiceless approach enables us to resolve the puzzle with just two players.

We employed density functional theory (DFT) to investigate the electronic structure of the semiconductor cubanite (CuFe$_2$S$_3$). Our findings reveal that the material exhibits an orbital-selective Mott insulator state, characterized by a band gap of 0.25 eV. This gap arises from strong electron-electron interactions acting specifically on the $d$-orbitals of iron, while the sulfur $p$-orbitals and copper $d$-orbitals remain largely unaffected. Consequently, the resulting magnetic structure aligns with experimental observations, and the calculated orbital densities match those derived from angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) data. Furthermore, our results indicate that the magnetic anisotropy in this system is driven by the distinct behavior of these orbitals.

We present a theoretical investigation of the Rabi oscillations exhibited by dark excitons in a quantum dot under biexciton conditions. Our analysis indicates that these dark exciton Rabi oscillations are contingent upon the alignment of biexciton and triplet spin configurations. Furthermore, our findings demonstrate that a magnetic field is required to induce Rabi oscillations within the specific subspace comprising the triplet and dark exciton states.

We introduce a two-dimensional wallpaper lattice characterized by a glide-symmetry-protected Dirac cone. By introducing dimerization within the glide-symmetry-breaking unit cell, we demonstrate the tunable destruction of the Dirac point via an opening direct gap. Furthermore, through symmetry-compatible lattice deformation, we achieve the conversion of Dirac semimetals into chiral or valley Chern bands. Our proposed model offers a pathway for engineering Dirac and Chern states in non-symmorphic lattices, potentially enabling the design of novel topological materials.

This paper introduces a new class of quantum states termed single-photon catalyzed coherent states (SPCCS). These states are generated by applying a single-photon operation to a coherent state, an approach that yields a state vector distinct from those produced by standard single-photon addition. We demonstrate that the statistical properties of these states, specifically their photon number distribution, can be effectively manipulated by adjusting the amplitude of the underlying coherent state. Furthermore, we calculate the Mandel Q parameter to illustrate the non-classical character of the SPCCS. Finally, we assess the quantum coherence and single-photon nature of these states, revealing that single-photon addition significantly enhances their quantum properties.

This paper introduces the application of bivectors within the Newman-Penrose formalism to represent the complex electromagnetic invariants and the five Weyl scalars. By utilizing the algebraic properties of bivectors, we derive the complex self-dual null tetrad and demonstrate how the electromagnetic stress-energy tensor and the Weyl curvature can be expressed in terms of these invariants and scalars, respectively.

Inferring the polymer sequence from its folding pattern is a significant challenge in polymer chemistry. This study introduces a new methodology that addresses this issue by initially applying linear regression to identify a linear mapping between monomer types and folding sequences. Subsequently, Integer Linear Programming is utilized to pinpoint the optimal integer sequence that adheres closely to the regression-derived mapping. We demonstrate that this approach successfully reconstructs the sequences of several well-known polymers, including the classic $\alpha$-helical peptide GLA-AVP, the immunoglobulin domain of streptococcal protein G, and the fibronectin type III domain.

Dynamic optimization serves as a powerful tool for solving time-evolving problems, offering superior performance compared to model predictive control by delivering longer-horizon solutions. This tutorial introduces direct transcription methods, which convert continuous-time optimization problems into discrete numerical formats solvable by algorithms like interior-point or sequential quadratic programming. To illustrate these concepts, we examine dual-patient mechanical ventilation, a strategy developed during the COVID-19 pandemic to support two critically ill individuals on a single device. This approach demonstrates how direct transcription facilitates rigorous, data-driven validation of such innovative solutions.

Delineating esophageal tumors in CT scans is a critical step for cancer treatment planning, yet it remains a significant challenge due to the irregular shapes of these lesions, the scarcity of distinguishable anatomical landmarks, and the difficulty in differentiating tumor tissue from surrounding structures. To address these issues, we propose a novel Deep Learning segmentation model named DDAUnet (Dilated Dense Attention Unet). This architecture integrates several key innovations: a Dense Unet backbone to enhance feature reuse, dense skip connections to preserve high-resolution spatial details, dilated convolutions to expand the effective receptive field, and a Dense Connected Convolutional Attention (DCCA) module. The DCCA module functions by aggregating both shallow and deep features to generate a refined feature map, which is then employed to isolate tumor regions. Evaluated on a specialized esophageal tumor dataset, DDAUnet achieved a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 0.818 and a 95% Hausdorff 95 distance (H95) of 3.411 mm. These outcomes surpass those of other state-of-the-art models, demonstrating the method's superior efficacy in segmenting esophageal tumors.

This study introduces a workflow for real-time well control and guidance that integrates well log interpretation with uncertainty quantification. Central to this approach is the use of an ensemble method for inverting well logs, which simultaneously characterizes formation properties and quantifies their uncertainty. The resulting formation property uncertainty is then incorporated into the risk assessment for geosteering decisions. To demonstrate the method's efficacy, a 3D numerical reservoir simulation is employed to generate synthetic well logs, illustrating the inversion and decision-making processes.

Named entity recognition (NER) stands as a core task in natural language processing, with nested NER representing a significant extension that has garnered considerable attention. In this study, we reframe nested NER as holistic structure parsing, a perspective that, to our knowledge, has not been previously explored. We introduce a new, efficient, and straightforward algorithm designed specifically for square nested structures. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that this approach achieves state-of-the-art performance across three major English benchmarks: CoN18, BioN18, and Chron18.

This paper examines the tropicalization of the moduli space of genus-4 curves and utilizes the resulting tropical enumerative theory to analyze bitangents to tropical quartics. We demonstrate that a bitropical quartic possesses exactly 28 bitangents, a figure that aligns with the classical count for algebraic quartics. Furthermore, we establish a correspondence between the bitangents of a tropical quartic and those of an underlying algebraic quartic; this result confirms the rationality of the enumerating count of bitangents for any specific quartic curve.

This study introduces a novel localization framework designed for wireless sensor networks. It addresses the challenge of pinpointing node positions when interference from other technologies distorts received signal strength (RSSI) measurements. The proposed method relies on the fact that while cross-technology interference alters RSSI values, it does not affect the physical geometry of the signal propagation. Consequently, the framework employs a geometric approach to determine positions, utilizing a specific algorithm to identify the most suitable anchor nodes. This selection process ensures that the calculated position is geometrically consistent with the actual positions of the chosen anchors. Experimental results indicate that this method achieves a localization accuracy of 0.5 meters.

Multilingual communities are increasingly prevalent, yet the scarcity of natural language processing (NLP) tools tailored for their mixed languages creates a significant barrier. This paper introduces a new benchmark dataset comprising over 1.5 million tweets from multilingual India, which we analyze to explore the complexities of these societies. We evaluate various models using this dataset to assess their performance on code-switched (CS) and code-mixed (CM) tasks, including character-level and document-level classification, as well as named entity recognition. Our analysis reveals that models struggle with CS and CM data, achieving only 50% to 60% of their standard monolingual accuracy. Furthermore, we identify that the prevalence of out-of-vocabulary words and the lack of adequate multilingual training data are key factors hindering success. To address these issues, we propose a new multilingual pre-training strategy that significantly improves results on code-switched and code-mixed data.

Automatic image description models are typically assessed using human-generated references, such as those from the Microsoft COCO dataset. However, this evaluation approach relies on a relatively small number of descriptions per image, which may not accurately represent natural language usage. To address this discrepancy, we introduce a method that creates large-scale human descriptions by sampling from existing small references. We demonstrate that this new, expanded dataset yields more reliable evaluations for automatic description models compared to traditional datasets.

Tantalum oxides ($Ta_2O_5$) are renowned for their exceptional dielectric breakdown strength, making them a leading candidate for next-generation high-voltage power electronics. Despite this, their crystal structure remains a subject of debate, with researchers proposing two distinct arrangements: a monoclinic structure (P2$_1$/c) and a rhombohedral structure (R$\bar{3}$c). To resolve this discrepancy, we conducted a comparative analysis of the formation energies for both models using density functional theory (DFT). Our DFT results indicate that the rhombohedral R$\bar{3}$c structure possesses a lower formation energy than the monoclinic P2$_1$/c structure, suggesting it is the more stable ground state. Furthermore, we performed Monte Carlo simulations to determine the equilibrium crystal structure under varying pressures. These simulations revealed that the rhombohedral R$\bar{3}$c structure remains stable up to 100 GPa, whereas the monoclinic P2$_1$/c structure transforms into the rhombohedral R$\bar{3}$c structure at approximately 10 GPa. Consequently, our findings support the conclusion that the rhombohedral R$\bar{3}$c structure represents the true ground state of tantalum pentoxide.

This study examines how geographic sorting on Reddit influences the spread of misinformation. Utilizing data from r/news, we analyzed over 1.5 million posts and found that the circulation of false news is significantly driven by the platform's major sorting mechanism, Big Geographic Sort (BigGeo). Specifically, BigGeo concentrates the dissemination of misinformation within specific regional clusters, whereas other sorting methods do not exhibit this pattern. These results suggest that understanding the role of algorithmic sorting is essential for developing effective strategies to mitigate the circulation of fake news.

In an era where malicious activities are increasingly concealed within seemingly normal behavior, identifying such suspicious events is more critical than ever. This paper introduces a novel detection framework designed to analyze rapid information streams, with a specific focus on uncovering suspicious content amidst benign data. The proposed method operates in two distinct stages. Initially, it employs a sliding window technique to segment continuous information flows into discrete, manageable windows. Subsequently, the framework extracts features from these windows and leverages a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to classify the data as either suspicious or normal. To validate the approach, we conducted experiments using Twitter datasets containing both benign and malicious content. The results demonstrate that this framework achieves a high F1-score, confirming its effectiveness in detecting suspicious information within fast data streams.

Human teachers often rely on speech to guide robots during task demonstrations, utilizing speech-act patterns that highlight key actions and objects. This study investigates the acoustic characteristics of speech used by humans to instruct robots on manipulation tasks. We analyzed three datasets: one featuring a teacher instructing a HuggingPoint robot, and two others with teachers guiding the Socially Assistive Robot (SAR) and the HRP-4C robots. Our analysis reveals that the acoustic features of instructional speech vary significantly depending on the specific robot being taught. Furthermore, we identified consistent acoustic patterns within each dataset that effectively distinguish between language highlighting objects versus actions. These findings suggest that automatic systems can leverage acoustic cues to identify the structural organization of human demonstrations.

Drawing inspiration from the uniform generation method for $n$-ary trees proposed by Raney in 1960, we introduce an algorithm that creates random trees by selecting them stochastically from the set of all possible $n$-tuples, where each position in the tuple can contain a different type of node.

Defining quantum complexity is a significant challenge, particularly within conformal field theories (CFTs). In this study, we examine the structure of complexity growth for both holographic and non-holographic CFTs in $1+1$ dimensions. We establish a mapping between the growth rate of complexity and the Euler-Arnard equations associated with the dual gravitational geometry in holographic scenarios, or the equations of motion for linearized gravitational perturbations in non-holographic cases. By leveraging these relationships, we derive explicit formulas for complexity growth in various $1+1$-dimensional models, including the $AdS_3/CFT_2$ duality framework, the Lee-Ying model, and theories exhibiting shockwave geometries.

Conversational agents are increasingly utilized to facilitate human interaction, yet developing and validating these systems remains challenging. We introduce CoaTe, an extensible framework designed for the efficient creation of regression test suites for conversational agents. This framework enables testers to define tests using a straightforward natural language syntax, which is then translated into executable test cases. We demonstrate the framework's effectiveness by building a comprehensive test suite for the Replika conversational agent. Our findings indicate that CoaTe is highly efficient, reducing the time required to author tests by 75% compared to manual methods.

The potential existence of a massive Planet X has been proposed to explain the orbital clustering of distant Kuiper Belt objects. This paper investigates whether the gravitational influence of such an object could be identified through the orbital dynamics of the Solar System's major planets. We specifically analyze the orbits of the eight known planets, focusing on the likelihood of detecting mass-induced perturbations in the semi-major axes and inclinations of the giant planets. Our findings indicate that, contrary to previous assumptions, the orbital data of the giant planets are sufficiently precise to constrain the mass of Planet X. Consequently, the proposed mass of approximately 10 Earth masses is inconsistent with current observations, as the data restricts the mass to less than 0.002 Earth masses (at 95% confidence).

The M-TM system constructs a memory bank by indexing a large corpus of sentences from the target language, enabling the model to retrieve and reuse similar sentences during translation. We examine the imprint of Conformal Cyclic Cosmology (R. Penrose, 2006) on the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) sky, analyzing both standard cosmological anomalies and potential new signatures. Our findings indicate that the CMB's large-scale dipole, quadrupole, and octupole anomalies can be explained by the influence of a low-energy, long-lived "aeon" from the preceding cycle. Furthermore, we explore the possibility of identifying Hawking radiation from evaporating primordial black holes as evidence for this prior aeon.

Few-shot learning aims to generalize effectively on tasks with very limited labeled data by leveraging training from broader data distributions. A prevalent strategy in this domain involves generating prototypes that represent entire classes. However, our analysis indicates that prototypes derived from standard datasets often suffer from suboptimal performance when applied to few-shot scenarios. To address this, we propose a novel framework for learning prototypes specifically tailored to few-shot contexts. Our approach utilizes a data augmentation technique to create an abundant supply of synthetic examples for each class during the prototype generation phase. Furthermore, we employ a two-stage curriculum learning framework: initially, prototypes are trained on these synthetic few-shot examples, followed by fine-tuning using prototypes learned from natural images. Experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art results.

Addressing the inherent sparsity in aspect-based recommendations, we introduce Multi-Sparse-Domain Collaborative Recommendation (MSDRCR). This framework leverages cross-domain information to mitigate data sparsity while simultaneously enhancing the modeling of diverse user interests through multi-sparse-domain collaboration. Specifically, we propose an Improved Comprehensive Aspect Preference Learning (ICAPL) module. This module refines aspect preferences by integrating explicit user interactions, implicit contextual information, and domain-specific knowledge. Furthermore, we define an optimization objective function and solve it using an efficient alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Extensive experiments conducted on two real-world datasets confirm that our approach significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

Hypatia is a specialized conic optimization solver designed to address problems formulated with the Hypatia.jl framework. This framework serves as an extension of the general-purpose Hypothesis.jl package, which supports the formulation of mixed-integer nonlinear programs (MINLPs). While Hypothesis.jl relies on the Ipopt solver for its nonlinear components, Ipopt lacks native support for conic structures; consequently, Hypothesis.jl's performance degrades when solving conic problems. In contrast, Hypothesis.jl allows users to define problems using Ipopt-compatible syntax, whereas Hypothesis.jl provides a dedicated syntax specifically for conic formulations. This distinction enables the deployment of efficient conic solvers like MOSEK, thereby significantly improving performance on problems that can be expressed in conic form.

Automated quality control (QC) for brain MRIs is essential for large-scale neuroimaging analysis, yet it remains difficult due to the need to learn from noisy data and generalize to unseen sites. We introduce a deep learning-based QC framework that predicts both binary acceptability and site-specific attributes (such as motion and resolution). This model was trained on 1.5T and 3.0T scans from a single site and evaluated on a diverse external test set comprising scans from 11 different institutions with varying protocols. The binary acceptability classifier achieved a macro F1 score of 0.91 on the external data, demonstrating robustness to significant domain shifts. Additionally, the model successfully identified eight out of ten types of non-anatomical artifacts and accurately localized seven out of ten types of anatomical issues. Finally, we assessed the utility of the learned site attributes for domain adaptation by retraining the model using site labels as auxiliary information; this approach yielded a 10% improvement in acceptability performance on the external dataset.

This paper investigates the impact of privately owned electric vehicles (POEVs) on distribution system resilience. A Multi-Agent Optimization (MAO) framework is proposed to model the decision-making processes of POEV drivers and utility companies. Specifically, drivers determine charging strategies to satisfy their energy needs while minimizing costs, whereas utilities decide on charging infrastructure placement and outage restoration sequences. The proposed model is non-convex, reflecting the intricate interactions between these stakeholders. To address this complexity, a solution algorithm is developed that combines a Branch-and-Check (B&C) approach with a heuristic method. Numerical simulations conducted on the IEEE 33-bus test feeder demonstrate that the proposed B&C algorithm converges rapidly and yields results within 0.5% of the heuristic solution. Furthermore, resilience analyses reveal that while a suboptimal restoration strategy may suffice for traditional systems, it becomes inadequate when POEVs are integrated.

This paper examines the performance characteristics of the Intel Optane DC Persistent Memory Module, a 256 GB memory device that functions as a high-speed, high-bandwidth, byte-addressable, and hardware-managed non-volatile memory (NVM) alternative to traditional storage. We conducted extensive evaluations using industry-standard benchmarks and custom applications to analyze the module's behavior. Our findings reveal that the device delivers random read/write speeds comparable to enterprise SSDs, while offering significantly higher bandwidth and lower latency than other NVM solutions. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the DC PM module effectively supports persistent heaps and persistent databases with minimal software modifications.

This paper introduces a new approach to the constrained rendezvous problem, where autonomous mobile agents must meet at a predetermined location. We propose a control scheme utilizing nonholonomic unicycles equipped with local recurrence drives. In this framework, each agent maintains a target relative position and velocity relative to its neighbors, motivated by an internal drive that ensures movement until reaching the rendezvous point. We demonstrate that this multi-agent system achieves both practical stability and convergence to the desired meeting location. Furthermore, we establish that the proposed method is more resource-efficient than existing solutions.

This study investigates the structural, electronic, and magnetic properties of GdSn$_3$, CmSn$_3$, and Gd$_x$Cm$_{1-x}$Sn$_3$ compounds within the AuCu$_3$-type structure using the full-potential linearized augmented plane wave (FP-LAPW) method. Our findings indicate that GdSn$_3$ and CmSn$_3$ exhibit non-magnetic ground states, whereas the Gd$_x$Cm$_{1-x}$Sn$_3$ solid solution displays ferromagnetic behavior. Furthermore, the calculated formation energy for Gd$_x$Cm$_{1-x}$Sn$_3$ is negative, confirming its thermodynamic stability. The negative formation energy indicates that Gd$_x$Cm$_{1-x}$Sn$_3$ is thermodynamically stable. We present a novel application of the AdS/CFT correspondence to predict the masses of heavy baryons and mesons within the Standard Model. By utilizing a bottom-up approach, we constructed a five-dimensional effective theory comprising two new gauge fields: a $U(2)$ "flavor" group and a $U(1)$ "color" group. This framework successfully predicts the mass spectrum for a wide range of hadrons, including the top quark, and aligns well with experimental data.

Weak gravitational lensing magnification is a key observable for studying the matter distribution of the universe, yet it remains challenging to measure directly. This study utilizes the Pantheon sample of 1050 Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) to analyze magnification by leveraging the known distances of these objects. We employ a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) approach to infer the amplitude of matter clustering, specifically the linearly extrapolated matter density contrast $\sigma_8\Omega_m^{0.6}$, using the $H_0$ value of $67.4$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$ from the Planck mission. Our analysis yields a value of $0.284 \pm 0.012$, which is consistent with the Planck results. Additionally, we investigate the impact of the distance ladder on the distance scale, finding that the measurement is robust against systematic uncertainties in $H_0$ derived from Planck data.

These lecture notes were prepared for a mini-course at the 2019 Summer School in St. Petersburg. They provide an accessible introduction to the theory of stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs) and their deterministic counterparts. The notes cover the fundamental existence and uniqueness results for both classical and mild solutions, as well as the connection between them. Additionally, they present the theory of stochastic convolution, which serves as the stochastic equivalent of deterministic semigroups. Finally, the core methodology for analyzing SPDEs—the fixed point argument—is introduced.

Defining and characterizing T centers in silicon remains a significant challenge, yet they are promising candidates for realizing room-temperature silicon-based quantum networks. This study presents the first comprehensive analysis of the T center's optical properties within a 3D photonic silicon-on-insulator framework. We demonstrate that the T center exhibits a strong photoluminescence signal peaking at 760 nm, which is highly sensitive to the local electric field. Furthermore, we identify optimal conditions for maximizing spin readout fidelity by evaluating the zero-field Lamb-Dicke parameter and the zero-field single-shot readout performance.

This study introduces an automated framework designed to detect brain tumors within MRI scans. The proposed system integrates image enhancement, segmentation, and color mapping techniques to achieve its objectives. Initially, the system applies histogram equalization to improve image contrast, utilizing the CLAHE algorithm to equalize contrast across localized regions. Subsequently, the K-Means clustering algorithm segments the images to isolate tumor areas. Finally, the system employs the HSV color model to visualize the detected tumors in color. Experimental outcomes indicate that this automated method is both efficient and effective.

We introduce an algebraic formulation of the degenerate Bernoulli numbers and examine their fundamental properties. By applying the theory of umbral algebra, we derive closed-form expressions for the associated twisted versions using both convolution and non-convolution polynomial forms. Additionally, we establish several recursive relations specific to the twisted entity. Finally, we generalize these concepts by defining A-twisted degenerate Bernoulli numbers within an arbitrary commutative ring that contains an inverse for the degeneracy parameter $\varepsilon$.

Stellar activity remains a significant obstacle in the search for exoplanets, often creating a measurement instability known as "activity jitter" that rivals or exceeds the signals of many small planets. This study evaluates the efficacy of line-based least-squares deconvolution (LSD) techniques for mitigating such effects. By applying two distinct randomised line selection algorithms to the active star HD 179949, the research demonstrates that these methods can substantially reduce activity-induced noise. Furthermore, the paper investigates the influence of line-list parameters, specifically the equivalent width (EW) cutoff, on LSD results. The findings reveal that the chosen line list has a critical impact on the stability of activity indicators and the precision of rotational measurements. Ultimately, the research advocates for the adoption of randomised line selection schemes to ensure consistent LSD performance across varying line lists.

This paper introduces a novel, link-quality-based approach for on-demand data collection in Wireless Sensor Networks (WDNs). This Hierarchical Range Sectoring and Bidirectional Link Quality Estimation (HRB) method organizes the collection process into multiple tiers, where each tier comprises distinct sectors within specific geographic ranges. To support this structure, the Bidirectional Link Quality Estimation (BIQDE) algorithm estimates the quality of links between nodes and the collector. By leveraging hierarchical range sectorization and bidirectional link quality estimation, HRB significantly reduces both data collection latency and energy consumption. Furthermore, the algorithm is designed to be flexible, accommodating various routing protocols and data aggregation techniques.

Deep object detectors have achieved remarkable success, yet their performance is often hindered by the inclusion of irrelevant background information. To address this, we introduce a new metric for assessing deep detectors that evaluates their sensitivity to contextual information. This metric measures the metric by determining the minimum amount of surrounding context required to cause a misclassification. We evaluate this metric on the PASCAL VOC 2010 dataset and compare it against two other established methods. Our analysis reveals that the proposed metric is superior for distinguishing between different deep detectors. Furthermore, we utilize this metric to evaluate various data augmentation strategies and to determine the optimal number of classes for multi-task learning.

This paper investigates a Kirchhoff-type elliptic system featuring a potential and terms with singular Trudinger-Moser growth. By leveraging the concentration-compactness principle adapted for singular integrals, we demonstrate the existence of at least one ground state solution.

This paper examines concentration inequalities for specific types of binary random variables exhibiting negative dependence. It begins by establishing a new, straightforward bound for the sum of negatively associated Bernoulli variables. Furthermore, it addresses variables defined on a partially ordered set that possess the negative cyclic dependence property, deriving a corresponding concentration inequality for their aggregate sum.
